history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery of the Drukpa Kagyu school. Founded in 1969 by the 8th Khamtrul Rinpoche, Dongyu Nyima, on 37 acres at Tashi Jong ('Auspicious Valley'), after the community fled Kham (eastern Tibet) in 1958 and first settled in Kalimpong, West Bengal. The complex includes the main temple (woodcarving, gilding, murals; statues including Shakyamuni Buddha), the stupa of Khamtrul Rinpoche, the restricted Yamantaka retreat centre, the Khampagar Monastic Institute, the Dorzong nunnery and a Tibetan craft emporium; the community practices ascetic yoga in the Mahamudra tradition. No monastery-specific festival calendar found in consulted sources (festivals left empty - verify). CORRECTION: CSV town 'Palampur' is approximate; the monastery is in the village of Tashi Jong between Paprola and Taragarh, ~15 km from Palampur. Coordinates from geocoding the monastery address (Palampur 176061).

name: Tashi Jong Monastery
town_description: Tashi Jong ('Auspicious Valley') is a small village between Paprola and Taragarh in Kangra district, ~15 km from Palampur, home to a Tibetan refugee settlement and monastery community.

travel.railway: Narrow-gauge Kangra Valley line serves the Palampur area; nearest broad-gauge railhead: Pathankot
travel.road: ~15 km from Palampur by road; ~10 km from Baijnath

visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours; monastery prayer schedule varies - verify locally
